question: On fresh fp28 curves, does prime-abscissa:size=304 + mitm:negation_folded=1 + targets=stride-renew-deferred-guard have lower counted cost S than the walk incumbent (size=407, targets=walk) at every weight w in {0, 0.1, 1} of the section 5a band, on the ea8e9ef7 executable?

claims.text: On fresh fp28 curves, prime-abscissa:size=304 + mitm:negation_folded=1 + targets=stride-renew-deferred-guard has lower counted cost S than the walk incumbent (size=407, targets=walk) at every weight of the section 5a band (w = 0, 0.1, 1), within ic.pipeline, max_trials 26479085, linalg incremental-gauss, the pinned executable and accounting as emitted. A recipe-level, constant-factor, counted claim; not asymptotic, not wall time, not rho-beating.

claims.if_not_supported: not supported within scope at the stated weights; close C1 route A at fp28 (weaken), or refuted at a common adverse weight; route B roadmap rule applies

claims.text: Within stride-renew at equal N (407 and 304), the deferred guard has equal counted S at w = 0 (both intervals inside [0.995, 1.005]) and lower counted S at w = 0.1 and 1. A component result, not an improvement of the IC baseline under section 5a.
claims.if_supported: reported as a native-work component saving outside tables A-C

hypotheses.statement: On fresh fp28 curves, the candidate recipe (size 304, stride-renew-deferred-guard) has lower counted S than the walk incumbent (size 407) at every weight w in {0, 0.1, 1} of the section 5a band.
hypotheses.mechanism: M(N,w,g) = N(N+1) + (1 + w k_g) T407 407/N + F + w G(N): a smaller N cuts the N(N+1) set-up, trials grow about as 1/N, and the deferred guard halves the per-trial native work (k_deferred = 1 against k_eager = 2) while leaving the target stream unchanged. Measured inputs: set-up N(N+1) exact, k_eager 2.0, F 0.19 S.

instance_sampling.rule: 120 workloads = 2 seeded fp28 prime_search curves x 60 public targets from target_seed, fixed before any data; the same workloads for every arm

blinding.how: Not masked. The metric is a deterministic count, so no analyst choice remains: analyze-c1.sh is frozen by sha256 before the data, and, before S2 writes job-exit.json, S1 is read only for transport and identity integrity (the check_job.py set, PROTOCOL section 9 step 2); audit, replay, invalid outcomes, A/A exactness, the pc-fb2x gate and parity run after S2 in the frozen analyze-c1.sh (runbook step S03). The blind control is the reviewer's re-derivation of the primary ratio (section 9 step 4).

power.note: Test-specific power of the paired, workload-clustered ratio, rerun at T = 60 targets per curve (120 workloads x 8 rounds, 10,800 executions per session). The experiment_protocol.py power command checks only rank-test p-value resolution (it passes at n = 960 trivially), so rank_test_n is null. The decision is an intersection-union test: all 3 weights x 2 sessions must reject at one-sided 0.025, so no multiplicity correction is applied (Berger, 1982); tests_in_family 6 with correction other for the checker. Variance inputs: two design-size local runs on non-study curves (24 workloads x 8 rounds, checks/dev/power1 and power2, ecbench compare incumbent->candidate at w = 0, 0.1, 1); U = hat + max(t half-width, bootstrap half-width); half-widths and sd scaled by true/observed ratio and by sqrt(24/120); sd from the t-CI (optimistic) and from the bootstrap CI/1.96 (conservative). Single-session power for a 3 % true effect (ratio 0.97) at w 0 / 0.1 / 1, conservative sd: power1 0.977 / 0.963 / 0.845; power2 0.951 / 0.944 / 0.838; optimistic sd: power1 0.999 / 0.997 / 0.942; power2 0.977 / 0.972 / 0.890. Minimum over both inputs, both sds and all weights: 0.838, so the rule (3 % power at least 0.8 at every weight) passes at T = 60 and the T = 72 fallback is not used. Both sessions must pass, so the joint two-session power at the minimum single-session value (0.838) is about 0.70 (0.838^2 = 0.702). At the projected effects (8.6 %, 10.6 %, 20.2 %) power is about 1.000. Approximate model (normal; the t quantile is kept at 23 degrees of freedom, which is conservative at 119); checks/p8r.py, p8r-out.txt.

the PROTOCOL section 10 rolling hard-bound gate: actual spend + HB(launch) + HB(every first-attempt job not yet launched) <= USD 5.00

deadline: a session that reaches its 3,600 s job deadline is an infrastructure outcome; the request is not rerun, no result is read from it, and it returns to the Coordinator (PROTOCOL section 9, deadline-hit rule)
an integrity or control gate failure (PROTOCOL section 7.3 steps 1 and 2), a parity failure, or an exit code outside 0, 42, 43 stops the session's verdict; it is never a negative result

invalidation_rules: an integrity or control gate failure (replay, audit, record count, invalid outcomes, spec or build equality, A/A twin not exact, pc-fb2x gate) makes the session invalid_measurement and not evidence
equal-N parity failure (section 5 rules 1 to 4) makes the session implementation_defect: a fix is opened and no scientific verdict is issued

a timeout, crash or host loss is infrastructure signal, not an empirical observation; the rerun rule is PROTOCOL section 9; a rerun uses the frozen launch/request-sK-r2.json, identical to request-sK.json except job.job_name, as a new runbook session after a Coordinator decision

decision_rule.text: Per session in order: integrity or control gate failure -> invalid_measurement; parity failure -> implementation_defect; U_w < 1 at every w in {0, 0.1, 1} -> pass; otherwise fail (fail_adverse at weights with L_w > 1). Overall: pass+pass supported_within_scope; fail+fail refuted_within_scope when a common weight is adverse in both, else not_supported_within_scope; pass+fail or fail+pass inconclusive; one valid and one invalid after the permitted rerun single_unreplicated (a pass gives analyzed, a fail gives weaken plus replication, never reject_scoped); implementation_defect in either session implementation_defect. PROTOCOL section 8.
decision_rule.threshold: U_w < 1 at each w in {0, 0.1, 1} in each of S1 and S2
decision_rule.statistic: ratio of mean counted S, candidate/incumbent, paired by algorithm_seed over 120 workloads x 8 rounds (ecbench compare --weight w, ops.ratio_b_over_a)
decision_rule.interval: 95 % CI, linearised t over workload clusters and cluster bootstrap (4000 resamples, seed 20261002); U_w = max of the two upper bounds, L_w = min of the two lower bounds
decision_rule.effect_size_measure: 1 - ratio at each w, with its CI
